CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Potato — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the potato as the shape-shifter of the tray — one vegetable wearing three costumes — and finds it hiding in plain sight.

What is this?

A potato is a brown root vegetable that grows underground, sold dusty from the field. Baked it is fluffy, fried it is golden sticks, mashed it is a cloud — one vegetable, three careers.

What does it mean?

Find the potato is a search with a twist: the shelf holds three potato foods, and the baked one in its brown jacket is the original costume.

What does the child need to know?

The three-costume game is the star: baked, fried, mashed cards side by side, one vegetable under all of them. Sorting foods by their source plant is real classification.

Why this matters

Potatoes feed more people than almost any crop on Earth, and the costume game explains every kids’ menu — the fries and the mash are the same friend in different clothes.

What it teaches

Source-to-food classification, costume sorting, and underground-growth curiosity.

Words to learn

potatobakedundergroundbrownfluffycostumes

Say this to your child

“A potato grows underground — dusty like a buried treasure! Crack it open: brown outside, cloud inside. Now look: fries are potatoes, mash is potatoes, this is a potato — one vegetable, three costumes! Which costume is dinner tonight?”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and find the split — brown jacket, white cloud inside. Tell the underground story: potatoes grow below, dusty from the garden soil. Then line up the three potato cards — baked, fries, mashed — and sort: same vegetable, three costumes! Match any real potato dish to its card before dinner.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the sort: the child who lines up three potato cards unprompted has done classification — the same skill behind every sorting game in the school.

Ask your child

Where do potatoes grow? What color is the jacket? Which cards are all potato? What is inside the split?

What your child can say or do

Underground! / Brown jacket. / Three costumes! / White cloud.

Out in the real world

Potatoes ride every meal plan and every garden bed — the costume game also explains hash browns, chips and gnocchi whenever they show up.

Try it together

Costume parade: deal the three potato cards face up, hold up a real potato dish or photo, and let the child match it to its costume — then swap plates and re-match.

Understanding check

Ask what three foods come from a potato. Baked, fries, mashed — any two named passes.

This lesson pairs with the Potato flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
